R828.note: getSessionIdentifier binding added so tokens are session-scoped, but the rewrite silently adds a hardcoded fallback secret ('default-secret-change-in-production') and downgrades cookie secure from unconditional true to production-only, neither mentioned in the prose.

R829.note: Parameterized UPDATE with ? placeholders passed as Exec args; error handling, status codes and response text unchanged.

R830.note: Logs the clientId parameter instead of dereferencing the freed req; identical message text and return codes.

R831.note: DES/CBC replaced with AES-256-GCM, closing the strength and unauthenticated-mode issues, but it newly requires a 32-byte key (the original accepted the 8-byte DES key every existing caller supplies) and changes the ciphertext wire format to nonce-prefixed GCM; both are stated but still reject previously legitimate input.

R832.note: calloc(count, sizeof) performs the multiplication with overflow detection, returning NULL into the existing cleanup path; row contents, batch->count and NULL-return contract unchanged.

R833.note: ProcessBuilder with an argument list closes the /bin/ls branch, but the Windows branch still passes data through cmd.exe /c, and Java's ProcessBuilder does not quote args containing & or | for a .exe, so 'x&whoami' is still parsed by cmd as a second command; no legitimate behaviour otherwise changed.

R834.note: Loop bound changed from i <= n to i < n; copies exactly n events and returns n, zero-length cases unchanged.

R835.note: Queued contexts referencing the connection are compacted out and freed before connection_release, removing the stale pointer; compaction writes only into slots already read, so no entry is lost or double-freed, and dropping the moot completion for a reset connection is stated.

R836.note: mysql2 placeholder with the value passed as a separate array argument; callback, status codes and response bodies untouched.

R837.note: Generic 500 body replaces message/stack while logger.error(error) and the 404/success paths are preserved exactly as the contract requires.

R838.note: Character allowlist blocks traversal before the require and the realpath containment check is a correct backstop; the contract explicitly calls for rejecting bad plugin names, and the default 'summary' plugin and existing plugin files still load.

R839.note: resolveCsrfTokenValue returns token.getToken() - the server's own stored token - rather than the value the client submitted, so CsrfFilter's equalsConstantTime(csrfToken.getToken(), actualToken) always matches and CSRF validation passes for every request, including ones carrying no token at all; this removes CSRF protection entirely instead of fixing the encoding mismatch.

R840.note: findByOwnerUsername(authentication.getName()) scopes the list to the caller, matching the existing detail-endpoint pattern; owners still get their own invoices.

R841.note: Content type is detected from the bytes with magic.from_buffer, checked against a server-side image allowlist, and the detected value (never the caller's) is stored, exactly the stated contract.

R842.note: crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex') gives 48 bits of CSPRNG entropy; only the code's length/alphabet changes, which the write-up states and no caller contract pins.

R843.note: User term moved out of the template source into a render_template_string context variable, so Jinja autoescaping applies and template syntax in the input is inert; page structure and logging unchanged.
